text.p: These are the leading stories in Albania's main newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOHA JONE
- An editorial says political and state arrogance under President Sali Berisha's administration is over following the June 29 general election.
- The leftist coalition of the Socialist Party, Social Democratic Party and Democratic Alliance Party, won more than two thirds of parliament, enabling it to push through vital legislation.

- A so-called committee of public salvation in Vlore, southern Albania, warned it would resume protests unless the Socialists, winner in the June 29 elections, agree to give people back the money they lost in pyramid investment schemes.
- The Democratic Party lost the recent poll mostly because of President Sali Berisha who was seen as largely responsible for the collapse of investment schemes.

- Leka Zogu, the heir of former Albanian King Ahmet Zog, told a crowd in Shkoder in the country's north that Albania's territorial integrity is at stake as Greece wants to control the south of the country.
- Some 60 children have been killed and another 800 injured due to stray bullets since March 1997.
- Many special unit forces and republican gurdsmen have quit the country after President Sali Berisha's Democratic Party was crushed in the election.
GAZETA SHQIPTARE
- The United States will help Albania get out of its deep economic crisis, President Bill Clinton told Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino during a meeting in Madrid.

- Three people died and dozens were injured in fighting between thousands of ethnic Albanian protesters and police in Macedonia on Wednesday. The violence broke out after police removed the Albanian national flag from the Gostivar town hall.
ALBANIA
- The paper says the new parliament will be the parliament of Kalashnikovs which should not be in charge of the constitution.
- The successor of king Leka Zogu accused the Socialist Party of manipulating the results of a referendum to restore the monarchy.

- The Legality Movement Party asked President Sali Berisha to stay in the office until the new government gives people back their money lost in pyramid investment schemes which collapsed early this year.
INDIPENDENT
- Republican Party and National Front Party vowed to help the leftist coalition in parliament to oust President Sali Berisha if he refuses to resign from office.
RILINDJA DEMOKRATIKE
- The revenge policies of the Socialist Party could threaten peace and stability in Albania, the paper said.
ZERI I POPULLIT
- Membership in NATO is an absolute priority of Albania's foreign policy, Prime Minister Bashkim Fino told the Madrid summit.
